name: interactive-pdf-binder
description: Print-first navigation system for assembled multi-document PDF binders on US Letter (612x792pt, origin bottom-left). One component, three navigation surfaces: slip-sheet TOC cover, TOC entry (active/inactive), and a HOME return button stamped on every content page. Rendered by tool-pdf-interactive.py (reportlab + pypdf) — not a DOM component; html/css below describe the design-system preview surface.

variants.name: slip-sheet
variants.description: Generated TOC cover page preceding each source document: header title, org subtitle, 1.5pt rule, optional right-aligned draft label (first sheet only), italic footer instruction. Holds up to 8 TOC entries per sheet (see oq-2 -- evidence suggests the real constraint is vertical space, not a row count).

variants.name: toc-entry-inactive
variants.description: Navigable TOC row for a non-current document: navy number + title, invisible full-rect GoTo link to that document's slip sheet.

variants.name: toc-entry-active
variants.description: TOC row for the current document: grey-light highlight rect, black text, a drawn 7.2x7.2pt filled-ink square marker (not a glyph -- see toc-group-header for why); no link (self).

variants.name: toc-group-header
variants.description: A row that labels a group of following child rows, e.g. 'Club Deals' over its member documents. Same 11pt Helvetica-Bold size as any other row, ink (not navy) since it isn't navigable, title case, no highlight/marker/link/rule. Takes the next number in sequence at toc-num-x; a clickable document can itself be a group header (a 'doc-parented' group, e.g. Schedules nested under the Long-Form Agreement they belong to) -- its own link rect narrows (toc-docparent-link-dy/height) so it can't overlap its first child's link rect. A group of exactly one document stays a plain numbered row -- a header over one child costs a line and groups nothing.

variants.name: toc-entry-child
variants.description: An unnumbered row nested under a toc-group-header: no number (the en-dash at toc-child-dash-x carries the position instead), title at toc-title-x plus one 18pt step, same colour/type/marker/link rules as a top-level entry. Rect is (toc-child-rect-x, y+toc-child-rect-dy, toc-child-rect-width, toc-child-rect-height) -- bracketing the text baseline, not the -25pt/24pt band some reference generators use (a bug: that band sits entirely below the baseline).

variants.name: home-button
variants.description: 54x14pt navy rounded-rect (3pt radius) with white INDEX label (renamed from HOME 2026-07-17 -- 'HOME' read as software/app vocabulary; 'INDEX' names the button's actual destination, the slip-sheet index, and matches the binder's own footer sentence), lower-right placement. Stamped on every content page (never slip sheets); transparent GoTo link to page 0 top.

aria: PDF-native accessibility, not ARIA — navigation is /GoTo link annotations plus a PDF document outline (/PageMode /UseOutlines), with /DisplayDocTitle true. A grouped TOC's visual nesting is mirrored structurally via add_outline_item(..., parent=...) -- for a doc-parented group this nested bookmark is the only machine-readable statement that the children belong to the parent document, not siblings of it. A group header is never its own link target (nothing new would be reached that its first child doesn't already reach); its bookmark resolves to that first child. Source PDFs are not guaranteed to be tagged; Tagged-PDF reading-order conformance for assistive technology is an open accessibility question (see open_questions), not yet handled by the generator.

wcag.note: Print/PDF target. Contrast: navy #002e63 on white ~13:1 (AAA); white on navy ~13:1 (AAA). Keyboard/assistive-tech navigation depends entirely on source-PDF tagging, which the current generator does not add. Known trade, flagged not resolved: the active-row marker moved from a text-layer glyph to a drawn graphic, so a screen-reader user's only cue for 'which tab am I on' is now the highlight shading plus ink-vs-navy text colour, not an extractable character.

open_questions: oq-1 (RESOLVED 2026-07-17): the earlier-suspected 7th color GREY_MID ('inactive entry subtitles') was confirmed absent from every production instance -- no binder renders subtitle rows. Stays dropped from this recipe.

oq-2: max 8 TOC entries per slip sheet is currently a hard limit in the generator. Evidence from a real 8-row slip sheet (MOU, 7 doc entries + 1 group header, ~4 rows of headroom to the footer) shows the real constraint is vertical space, not a row count -- a child row costs 26pt against a top-level row's 48pt, so a mixed page can hold more than 8 rows. Recommend re-expressing the cap as a computed space budget rather than a fixed count; not yet done.
oq-3: Tagged-PDF / reading-order conformance for assistive technology is currently unhandled — source PDFs pass through untagged.
oq-4 (RESOLVED 2026-07-17): navy pinned to #002e63 -- confirmed against the live Python source's exact RGB constant (0.0, 0.18, 0.39).

oq-5: no title wrapping or max-length guard anywhere in the generator -- a long title silently runs past its box's right edge. Should the recipe specify wrapping or a documented max length (~400pt / ~66 characters at the child level)?

oq-6: should a doc-parented group (a clickable document that is itself a parent, e.g. Schedules under an Agreement) ever nest more than one level deep? No production instance does; recommend capping at one until a real case exists.

oq-7 (landscape slip sheets): all current instances are portrait. Right-margin-dependent geometry is already expressed via margin-right rather than a literal value, so a landscape variant is lower-risk than it would otherwise be -- not built, not requested yet.
